data.description:
Found while validating mechanical-coherent-wolverine's premise.

## Report

`rebar._commands.txn.transition_core` declares `force_close_reason: str = ""` at src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:198 and NEVER READS IT. The identifier occurs exactly once in the whole file — the parameter declaration itself.

The caller does supply it: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py passes `force_close_reason=force_close` into the locked write. So the reason an operator typed into `--force=<reason>` is accepted, threaded one call deep, and silently dropped before it reaches the STATUS event.

## Why it matters

The close STATUS event records only `status`, `current_status`, `parent_status_uuid` and present-only `close_class` (txn.py:277-296). A force-close therefore leaves NO durable record of why a gate was bypassed, on the event that would naturally carry it.

There IS a best-effort FORCE_CLOSE audit comment written later in transition_close.py, but it is a separate write that acquires the lock again and is swallowed on failure — so under the contention that makes force-closing attractive in the first place, the bypass reason can vanish entirely while the parameter designed to carry it durably sits unused.

This is adjacent to mechanical-coherent-wolverine (23b2-1a94-6a01-466b), which needs the same STATUS event to start carrying completion-signature expectation. The two touch the same event and should probably be sequenced together, but they are distinct defects: this one is a dropped parameter, that one is a missing field.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The force-close reason supplied to transition_core reaches a durable record, or the parameter is removed as dead — verified by a test
- [ ] Whichever way it is resolved, no caller silently passes a value that is discarded — verified by a test
data.title: force_close_reason is accepted by transition_core and discarded
